oneliner.t: Tucson painting contractor and three-time Republican nominee in AZ-7 — he lost to Raúl Grijalva in 2024 and to Adelita Grijalva in the 2025 special — who speaks publicly about his recovery from addiction and prison time and backs the bipartisan Dignity Act on immigration.

born.t: 1966, Tucson, Arizona (per his own Ballotpedia survey)
born.note: Self-reported; KOLD gave his age as 58 in Oct. 2024, which is consistent.

upbringing.t: Says he was born in Tucson and calls himself a third-generation Arizonan. By his own account to KOLD, he was arrested in 1991 for possessing about a gram of marijuana, violated probation while awaiting trial, and served about 4½ years of a 10-year sentence; a court voided that conviction in 2020. He says he later used methamphetamine and crack cocaine, was homeless for years, served about four more years in prison, lost custody of his children, and has since found religion and recovered. He now owns a painting business and a horse rescue that employs people recently released from prison, and says his voting and gun rights have been restored. His sister died while homeless.

career.org: Horse rescue employing people recently released from prison

platform.t: Backs the bipartisan Dignity Act (more border security and judicial resources plus legal work status for long-term undocumented residents with clean records who pay penalties); supports more border-wall construction; calls ICE law enforcement that 'needs to be there'; wary of mass deportation because southern Arizona farms and businesses rely on immigrant labor.

Supports some Trump-proposed election changes, including federal administration of federal elections and the SAVE Act; opposes ending mail-in voting; says he does not share claims that elections lack integrity and that whether Trump won 2020 is not his focus.

Would seek federal grants for mandatory diversion programs modeled on Pima County's Drug Treatment Alternative to Prison; earlier proposed ending tax-funded methadone clinics, work camps for housing, and job programs where participants pay room and board.
Colorado River loss decisions should rest with local governments; new data centers should secure their own water before building.
Website lists tax cuts, tax-code reform, job growth and more Border Patrol resources (as reported by FOX 10).
Supports congressional term limits; parents, not government, should control curriculum; Second Amendment 'given by God'; refocus federal investigators on national security and cartels.

promises.t: Seek federal grants to expand mandatory drug-diversion programs.
Set partisanship aside and work across the aisle for the district.

research_notes: RACE HISTORY: 2024 general — lost to Raúl Grijalva 36.6%–63.4% (99,057 votes); 2025 special primary — won 60.9%; 2025 special general — lost to Adelita Grijalva 29.4% (29,944) to 68.9%; 2026 primary — 21,934 votes, unopposed. Ballotpedia found no endorsements in any of the three races. Ballot name: Daniel Francis Butierez, Sr. LEGAL CAUTION: all prison details come from his own on-record interviews and a court document he posted, as described by AZPM; no court record was opened, and the voided case must not be described as a standing conviction. Photo not retrieved.
